nodes.label: Security & privacy review report (0 CRIT/HIGH, 3 MED, 3 LOW, 6 INFO)
M1: circuit-profile array CPU-DoS
nodes.rationale: A hostile profile JSON within the 5 MB cap can pack ~80k centerline points and ~20k gates, driving O(gates x centerline) validation plus an O(gates^2) proximity loop (~1e9 ops) and a per-GNSS-fix full projection cost in TrackMatcher.match — latent until an import feature ships; fix is zod .max() caps and an O(n log n) neighbor check.

nodes.label: M2: unbounded in-memory session telemetry
nodes.rationale: rawSamples and pipelineCore's matches/rejectedSamples/stateHistory arrays grow one entry per GNSS fix for the whole session and are never trimmed; a multi-hour track day degrades memory and per-lap CPU on constrained iPhones. Fix: trim rawSamples to the in-flight lap and cap the diagnostic arrays with rolling windows.

nodes.label: M3: no user-facing location-data deletion path
nodes.rationale: deleteUserData is implemented correctly in sqlSessionRepository but never called from any screen, so precise driving-location history is kept indefinitely with no in-app removal; fix is wiring a Settings 'Delete my data' control to it.

nodes.label: L2: checkpoint deserialization validates envelope only
L3: unused expo-task-manager dependency
nodes.rationale: Declared but never imported; contradicts the foreground-only least-privilege posture and adds supply-chain surface for no benefit — removed until a background-location feature is deliberately decided.

nodes.label: Offline no-exfiltration posture (I3-I5 clean)
nodes.rationale: Zero fetch/XHR/WebSocket/axios call sites, no analytics or crash reporting, no console logging of coordinates, fully parameterized SQL, and least-privilege when-in-use location permissions — the review confirmed the offline-first privacy story end to end.

nodes.label: I1: iOS mock-location detection gap
nodes.rationale: Android mocked samples are dropped and counted, but expo-location exposes no iOS equivalent; a smooth spoofed track passes all checks. Accepted because the app is single-user local-only — impact is self-deception, revisit if sharing/leaderboards arrive.
